tenues: tenuis, -e — thin, slight, scanty, poor (m./f. nom./acc. pl.)
terrae: terra, -ae (f.) — earth, land, country (gen./dat. sg.; nom. pl.)
testor: testor, -ārī, testātus sum — to call to witness, swear by (1st sg. pres., deponent)
thybrim: Thybris, -idis (m.) — the Tiber (acc. sg., Greek form in -im)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
torquent: torqueō, -ēre, torsī, tortum — to twist, whirl (3rd pl. pres.)
totiens: totiēns (adv.) — so often, so many times
tristia: tristis, -e — grim, sad, bitter (n. acc. pl.)

troiae: Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (gen. sg.) · also dat. sg., for Troy (sīc fāta ferēbant)

tuis: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (m./n. abl./dat. pl.) · also f. abl./dat. pl. (tuīs querēlīs)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tuta: tūtus, -a, -um — safe, sheltered (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
tutum: tūtus, -a, -um — safe; in tūtum, to safety (n. acc. sg.) · also m. acc. sg., safe (tūtum tē, predicative)
ulla: ūllus, -a, -um — any (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.); with non, no
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
undae: unda, -ae (f.) — wave, water (nom. pl.; gen./dat. sg.)
unum: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single, the same (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
unus: ūnus, -a, -um — one, alone, a single (m. nom. sg.)
utraque: uterque, utraque, utrumque — each of two, both (f. nom. sg.)
vasto: vastus, -a, -um — vast, huge, desolate (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
velis: vēlum, -ī (n.) — sail; canvas, cloth, awning (abl./dat. pl.) · also volō, velle, voluī — to wish (2nd sg. pres. subj.: esse velīs)
venus: Venus, Veneris (f.) — Venus, goddess of love, mother of Aeneas (nom. sg.)
vertere: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, change, drive (pres. inf.)
vicissim: vicissim (adv.) — in turn, in succession, on the other hand
viribus: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, strength; pl. vīrēs, vīrium, strength (abl./dat. pl.)
vocantem: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, call upon (pres. part., m. acc. sg.)
volans: volō, -āre — to fly (pres. part., m. nom. sg.) · also f. nom. sg. (columba volāns)
xanthum: Xanthus, -ī (m.) — Xanthus, river of Troy (acc. sg.)
